title: Ever feel dizzy or faint
after standing in the heat too long?
3 Habits Behind Heat Syncope

items.name: Why do you suddenly feel dizzy or faint?
body: Heat widens your skin's blood vessels to cool you down,
pulling blood flow away from your brain -
these three habits make it drop even faster

items.name: Standing up too fast
body: Your vessels are already widened from the heat,
so they can't keep up with the sudden change

items.name: Stand up like this instead
body: Once you're up, stay put for a moment

items.name: Standing in direct sun too long
body: Blood pools in your legs instead of

items.name: In the heat, do this
body: Still have to stand? Pump your calves -
shift your weight or rock on your feet

items.name: Pushing through the warning signs
body: tunnel vision, or a cold sweat
already dropping - pushing through raises your risk

items.name: When the signs hit, do this
body: Sit or lie down right away and
raise your legs above heart level
sip water or a sports drink slowly

headline: Stand up slowly, take shade breaks,
and listen to the warning signs -
manage those three and heat syncope becomes far less likely
tip: Pause before standing, and rest in the shade often -
